https://www.tribtoday.com/news/local-new.text: News Local News Latest News Obituaries Business Community News Police Blotters Ohio News National News International News Sports Local Sports Sport columns High School Sports YSU Sports Ohio Sports National Sports Opinion Guest Columnists Editorials Letters to the Editor Life Lifestyles Ticket Society Burton Cole column Deals on Wheels Classifieds Garage Sales Jobs Contact Information Contact Us Advertise Subscribe Statement of Values Terms of Service Submit News Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Facebook Twitter Local News Howland OKs support for water trail extension By BRANDON CANTWELL August 13, 2026 2 min read Trending HOWLAND -- The Mahoning River has been a central focus in the area for the past few years at both the state and local level, and Howland trustees at Wednesday's meeting approved a resolution aimed at helping to promote its growth. Trustees approved providing a resolution of support for an application proposing to extend the Mahoning River Water Trail. The resolution states that Howland will join other entities such as Girard, Weathersfield, McDonald, Youngstown, Campbell, Struthers, Lowellville and Poland, as well as the Mahoning River Corridor Initiative and Mahoning River Corridor Mayors Association to extend it, to encourage tourism and eco-friendly, educational, historical, cultural and recreational activities on the river. The resolution, a version of which Girard officials passed at the city council meeting Monday, acknowledges that Howland fronts on the Mahoning River and is traversed by Mosquito Creek, one of the river's main tributaries, which provides "significant opportunities" for water-based recreation, wildlife observation and environmental education and conservation. The resolution states the participating communities recognize the long-term vision of extending the regional water trail network, by developing a future Mosquito Creek Water Trail from the dam to its meeting point with the Mahoning River. The new water trail is expected to enhance regional connectivity, public access, outdoor recreation and the Mahoning River's stewardship. Planning Director Kim Mascarella said the water trail will be extended all the way down through Lowellville. "There have been extensive upgrades to parks along the river, dredging of certain parts of the river, the removal of dams," Mascarella said. "That greatly enhances recreational opportunities all along the Mahoning River, and Mosquito Creek drains into the Mahoning River in the front, near Bolindale." Mascarella said the trail will extend from just Trumbull to both Trumbull and Mahoning counties, but she wasn't sure of its total acreage or linear mileage. Starting at /week. Subscribe Today

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cmy83w.text: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees Close People evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky were reunited with their loved ones after crossing from Belarus into Ukraine on Saturday. This comes as a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday. Families were reunited at a site in the region of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine after arriving in buses and ambulances. They had previously travelled via Crimea and Russia after their evacuation from the Ukrainian town on Friday. Ceasefire measures will remain in place until the end of Sunday 1 November. The BBC's Dan Johnson reports from the site in the Chernihiv region, near the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus. Read more on this story.
